chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Hajj is of three types: Hajj al-Mufrad, Hajj al-Qiran, and Hajj al-Tamattu' with Umrah until Hajj. And with these, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered, and the merit is in them, and we do not command the people except with them.'

key_terms.تَمَتُّعٍ: Hajj al-Tamattu': A type of Hajj where the pilgrim performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, and then enters Ihram again for Hajj.
key_terms.حَجُّ مُفْرَدٍ: Hajj al-Mufrad: A type of Hajj where the pilgrim enters the state of Ihram for Hajj only, without Umrah.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him and his family).
key_terms.قِرَانٍ: Hajj al-Qiran: A type of Hajj where the pilgrim combines Umrah and Hajj in a single Ihram.

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the three canonical forms of Hajj—Mufrad, Qiran, and Tamattu'—as the exclusive modes of pilgrimage commanded by the Messenger of Allah. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of these practices, asserting that the Imams did not introduce new categories but rather adhered strictly to the prophetic tradition, thereby validating the merit (al-fadl) inherent in these specific ritual structures.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Hajj is of three types – an individual Hajj, and a paired one (قِرَانٍ), and Tamatto (تَمَتُّعٍ) with the Umra to the Hajj, and Rasool-Allahsaww ordered with it, and the merits are therein, and weasws do not order the people except with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I have heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Al-Hajj is of three kinds: al-Mufrad al-Hajj (al- Hajj without al-‘Umrah), Qiran, and al-Tamattu £ , which is al- £ Umrah along with al-Hajj. This is how the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had commanded. This has excellence and we do not command people to complete an al-Hajj in a manner other than this (al-Tamaatu‘).’”
